vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: facebook-group-monitor
Version: 1.1.0

The facebook-group-monitor skill is a functional tool designed to scrape and monitor Facebook groups using Playwright browser automation. It features a transparent implementation in `scripts/fb-group-monitor.py` that handles session persistence, post extraction via JavaScript, and screenshot capture for AI vision analysis. The skill requires a one-time manual login to establish a session, avoiding the need to handle raw user credentials, and does not exhibit any signs of data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious intent.

llm.summary: The files and runtime instructions match the skill's stated purpose (Playwright-based Facebook group scraping with persistent login and optional screenshots); nothing in the package requests unrelated credentials or installs unexpected components.

dimensions.detail: Name/description promise Playwright-based Facebook group monitoring; included Python and shell scripts implement Playwright, stealth mode, persistent session, screenshot capture, and seen-post tracking — all expected for this purpose. The setup doc explains installing Playwright/Chromium which is coherent with the functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits login to a one-time interactive terminal step (reduces credential exposure) and instructs using --shots-dir inside the agent workspace so the image tool can read screenshots. That is purposeful for LLM vision but increases where potentially sensitive images are stored and accessible to other agent tools — user should be aware and choose the shots directory carefully. No instructions ask the agent to read unrelated secrets or system paths.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automatic install spec; SETUP.md instructs manual venv and pip install of playwright and playwright-stealth plus running 'playwright install chromium' which downloads a Chromium binary (~150MB). This is expected but means the user will download and run a browser runtime managed by Playwright.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request any API keys, tokens, or unrelated environment variables. It optionally respects an FBMON_VENV env var to choose a venv, which is reasonable. The main sensitive artifact is the persistent browser profile (.browser-data) that stores logged-in session state; that is necessary for scraping but should be protected.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced global presence). The skill uses a persistent browser session (on-disk) to avoid re-login; this is expected for the functionality. Agent autonomous invocation is the platform default — note that once installed and provided access to the session data, the skill can run scrapes without interactive login.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to do what it says: it scrapes Facebook groups using Playwright and stores a persistent browser session. Before installing, consider: (1) keep the .browser-data directory private — it contains your Facebook session and can be used to access your account; (2) avoid running the login step from an automated agent — perform the one-time interactive login yourself; (3) choose the screenshots directory deliberately (saving screenshots in the shared agent workspace makes them available to other tools and may expose private content); (4) run the code inside an isolated virtual environment or container and review/maintain the selectors (Facebook DOM changes frequently); (5) if you plan cron/autonomous runs, ensure the schedule and scraping rate comply with Facebook's terms and avoid aggressive polling. If you want further review, provide the full (untruncated) fb-group-monitor.py so I can scan for any hidden network endpoints or unexpected behavior.
